investigator_character: Facilities automation and refrigeration maintenance technician who enjoys solving mysteries in spare time
in_world_duration: one night shift (approximately four in-world hours)
location_scale: single industrial warehouse and attached offices
content_boundaries: no graphic violence; no supernatural elements; adult workplace themes including negligence, fraud, and institutional pressure; no sexual content
required_themes: one perfect ending and several imperfect endings
author_notes: Codename: The Cold Storage Alarm. First real Generator v2 adventure. Setting: regional cold-chain distribution warehouse after hours. Central incident: critical cold-storage failure and unauthorized access alarms without obvious theft or violence. Bounded scale: five primary locations (loading dock, cold storage hall, automation control room, security office, warehouse manager office) with a staff break room as a secondary hub. Five primary NPCs (night security guard, on-call warehouse supervisor, refrigeration contractor, logistics coordinator, cleaning crew lead) plus badge-access records for a sixth IT administrator role without requiring a live interview. Investigation structure: technician called to diagnose an automation fault while storage temperature rises; fair paths through badge logs, building-management trend exports, refrigeration setpoints, witness statements, and physical inspection of doors, sensors, and override panels. Time pressure: rising storage temperature and an approaching write-off or compliance deadline closes interviews and deep inspections. Planned aha type: a routine maintenance timestamp that initially appears benign gains significance when correlated with an override sequence and access timing (delayed significance; no early spotlight). At least one testimony-versus-evidence contradiction required between a witness account and badge or sensor records. Endings: one fully supported perfect reconstruction; several imperfect endings that preserve investigation rather than hard-stopping play. Failure routes redirect to continued inquiry. Incident design space: industrial negligence, unauthorized access, or financial fraud — resolution not fixed in this brief.
